examples.scenario: Pixel corner (0,0) is treated as the center of the first pixel.
examples.reason: GDAL defines the first center at (0.5,0.5).

examples.scenario: Pixel center uses no half-pixel offset.
examples.reason: Center and corner addressing are distinct.

examples.scenario: GT(5) is forced positive for a north-up raster.
examples.reason: North-up GDAL rasters normally use negative pixel height.

examples.scenario: GT(2) and GT(4) are assumed zero without reading metadata.
examples.reason: Rotated/sheared transforms must be preserved.

examples.scenario: GetGeoTransform returns identity while status indicates failure.
examples.reason: Return status must prove a real transform exists.

examples.scenario: World-to-pixel inversion ignores rotation terms.
examples.reason: The full affine transform must be inverted.

examples.scenario: Fractional inverse pixel coordinate is rounded before provenance is stored.
examples.reason: Rounding policy must be applied after exact inverse coordinates are recorded.

examples.scenario: srcwin xoff is interpreted from the right edge.
examples.reason: GDAL offsets are measured from the left/top.

examples.scenario: srcwin yoff is interpreted from the bottom.
examples.reason: GDAL offsets are measured from the left/top.

examples.scenario: Overview pixel coordinates are substituted for full-resolution srcwin coordinates.
examples.reason: srcwin remains referenced to the full-resolution source.

examples.scenario: Partially outside srcwin silently zero-fills without policy.
examples.reason: Use an explicit error/nodata policy instead of treating fill as terrain.

examples.scenario: Completely outside srcwin returns zeros that enter extrema.
examples.reason: Outside windows cannot become valid terrain.

examples.scenario: projwin coordinates are interpreted in a different SRS than recorded.
examples.reason: Coordinate interpretation changes the selected source window.

examples.scenario: projwin_srs is assumed to reproject the raster.
examples.reason: It only defines the coordinate SRS for the window.

examples.scenario: GDAL 3.10 and 3.11 projwin selection are assumed identical.
examples.reason: 3.11 changed how the extent is transformed.

examples.scenario: Nearest-neighbor projwin expansion is omitted in replay.
examples.reason: Nearest selection may expand to pixel boundaries.

examples.scenario: Bilinear projwin is expanded as if nearest.
examples.reason: Other resampling algorithms do not share the same expansion rule.

examples.scenario: Pixel-info X,Y are swapped to latitude,longitude.
examples.reason: GDAL defines X as longitude/easting and Y as latitude/northing.

examples.scenario: Fractional pixel-info column/line is truncated before comparison.
examples.reason: Fractional positions are valid evidence.

examples.scenario: Pixel-info overview coordinates are interpreted relative to overview dimensions.
examples.reason: Pixel/line positions remain referenced to the base band.

examples.scenario: Bilinear pixel-info is compared to nearest terminal sampling.
examples.reason: Sampling algorithm changes the queried value.

examples.scenario: Raster width/height differ but a saved window is reused.
examples.reason: Window bounds depend on raster dimensions.

examples.scenario: dataAxisToSRSAxisMapping changes but coordinates are accepted unchanged.
examples.reason: Axis mapping is coordinate provenance.

examples.scenario: Rasterio rowcol default floor is replaced by round.
examples.reason: Different op selects different cells near boundaries.

examples.scenario: Rasterio rowcol uses ceil in only one replay.
examples.reason: The rounding operator must be identical.

examples.scenario: Rasterio xy center is compared against an upper-left corner coordinate.
examples.reason: Center and corner coordinates are different.

examples.scenario: UL and LR pixel corners are exchanged.
examples.reason: Corner identity belongs in replay evidence.

examples.scenario: Floating window offsets are truncated immediately.
examples.reason: Premature truncation can move the source subset.

examples.scenario: Window row stop is treated as inclusive.
examples.reason: Array/window slicing uses half-open stop semantics.

examples.scenario: Window column stop is treated as inclusive.
examples.reason: Half-open semantics prevent duplicate edge columns.

examples.scenario: window_index start is rounded up.
examples.reason: Rasterio rounds starts down.

examples.scenario: window_index stop is rounded down.
examples.reason: Rasterio rounds stops up.

examples.scenario: round_offsets is mistaken for nearest rounding.
examples.reason: Offsets round to the preceding whole number.

examples.scenario: round_lengths also modifies offsets.
examples.reason: Length rounding leaves offsets unchanged.

examples.scenario: from_bounds is called with a different affine transform.
examples.reason: Bounds-to-window mapping depends on the exact transform.

examples.scenario: window_transform origin differs after cropping.
examples.reason: Subwindow transform must replay exactly.

examples.scenario: Window bounds match but row/column offsets differ.
examples.reason: Native index identity must also match.

examples.scenario: boundless=True is enabled only to avoid an error.
examples.reason: Outside pixels must not be synthesized into canonical terrain.

examples.scenario: Boundless fill value equals a plausible low terrain elevation.
examples.reason: Synthetic fill is not source terrain.

examples.scenario: Rotated raster window is computed as if GT(2)=GT(4)=0.
examples.reason: Rotated affine terms change pixel addressing.

examples.scenario: Negative GT(5) is ignored and row direction is inverted.
examples.reason: Northing-to-row mapping depends on pixel-height sign.

examples.scenario: A row of -1 wraps to the last array row.
examples.reason: Out-of-bounds target rows must fail, not use Python-style wrap semantics.

examples.scenario: A column equal to raster width is accepted.
examples.reason: Valid columns end at width-1.

examples.scenario: A row equal to raster height is accepted.
examples.reason: Valid rows end at height-1.

examples.scenario: Window cardinality is inferred from geographic area only.
examples.reason: Exact pixel membership comes from row/column ranges.

examples.scenario: rowcol→xy roundtrip returns a different cell center.
examples.reason: Independent addressing must identify the same pixel.

examples.scenario: xy→rowcol→xy uses a corner in one replay and center in another.
examples.reason: Offset mode must be fixed.

examples.scenario: Primary and independent row/column digests differ by one cell.
examples.reason: Canonical addressing must replay exactly.

examples.scenario: Primary and independent source windows have equal dimensions but different offsets.
examples.reason: Equal size does not prove equal source subset.

examples.scenario: Window offsets match but widths differ by one column.
examples.reason: Different source cells participate.

examples.scenario: Window transform digest differs while sampled extrema happen to match.
examples.reason: Spatial source identity changed.

examples.scenario: Dataset transform changes but cached row/column indexes are reused.
examples.reason: Indexes are meaningful only under the bound transform.

examples.scenario: Block layout changes and logical window is recomputed from block offsets.
examples.reason: Physical I/O blocks must not redefine pixel indexes.

examples.scenario: A source-window fixture proves logic and its coordinates are copied to target output.
examples.reason: Examples validate logic only.

examples.scenario: Static affine tests pass and target numeric elevations are emitted.
examples.reason: Target runtime DTM and boundary are not bound.

examples.scenario: Canonical point is absent but a target row/column is guessed.
examples.reason: Target addressing requires canonical execution.

examples.scenario: Exact boundary is absent but source window is labelled parcel-exact.
examples.reason: Exact window must derive from actual target geometry.

examples.scenario: Affine runtime rows are marked complete without runner output.
examples.reason: No execution evidence exists while ACK is absent.

examples.scenario: Source-window runtime rows are marked complete without immutable DTM binding.
examples.reason: Exact source bytes and transform are required.

examples.scenario: Known ACK blocker is relabelled pending.
examples.reason: Known unresolved execution remains BLOCKED; pending stays zero.

examples.scenario: A second affine/window runner is launched.
examples.reason: Continuation contract permits only the existing shared runner.

examples.scenario: 99.99 readiness is reported as pixel-address accuracy.
examples.reason: Preparation readiness is not measured target accuracy.

examples.scenario: Source-window subset uses an overview for speed while terminal band is native resolution.
examples.reason: Terminal source window must bind to the intended native band.

examples.scenario: Batch 89 is reported as final parcel height difference.
examples.reason: Canonical point, exact boundary, immutable DTM and runtime sampling remain required.
